problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
problems.statement:
You are given an integer array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i-th` day.

On each day, you may decide to buy and/or sell the stock. You can only hold at most one share of the stock at any time. However, you can buy it then immediately sell it on the same day.

Find and return the maximum profit you can achieve.

examples.explanation: Buy day 2 (1), sell day 3 (5), profit 4. Buy day 4 (3), sell day 5 (6), profit 3. Total 7.
Buy day 1 (1) and sell day 5 (5), profit 4.
Prices are strictly declining, no transaction done, profit 0.

commonMistakes: Trying to find global min and global max instead of capturing every positive price delta.
hints: Greedy observation: any upward slope `prices[i] - prices[i - 1] > 0` can be captured as profit.
Sum all positive daily increments `Math.max(0, prices[i] - prices[i - 1])`.

testCases.explanation: Stress test scale N=1000 for complexity verification
Stress test scale N=2000 for complexity verification

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III
problems.statement:
You are given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i-th` day.

Find the maximum profit you can achieve. You may complete at most two transactions.

Note: You may not engage in multiple transactions simultaneously (i.e., you must sell the stock before you buy again).

examples.explanation: Buy day 4 (price 0) and sell day 6 (price 3), profit 3. Buy day 7 (price 1) and sell day 8 (price 4), profit 3. Total 6.
Buy day 1 (price 1) and sell day 5 (price 5), profit 4.

commonMistakes: Using O(N^2) splitting loops instead of bidirectional DP or 4-state state machine.
hints: Track 4 states in a single pass: `buy1`, `sell1`, `buy2`, `sell2`.
`buy1 = max(buy1, -price)`, `sell1 = max(sell1, buy1 + price)`.
`buy2 = max(buy2, sell1 - price)`, `sell2 = max(sell2, buy2 + price)`.
Return `sell2`.

Stress test scale N=1500 for complexity verification

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock IV
problems.statement:
You are given an integer array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i-th` day, and an integer `k`.

Find the maximum profit you can achieve. You may complete at most `k` transactions: i.e. you may buy at most `k` times and sell at most `k` times.

Note: You may not engage in multiple transactions simultaneously (i.e., you must sell the stock before you buy again).

examples.explanation: Buy day 1 (price 2) and sell day 2 (price 4), profit 2.
Buy at 2, sell at 6 (profit 4). Buy at 0, sell at 3 (profit 3). Total profit 7.

commonMistakes: Not optimizing for `k >= n / 2` (which reduces to Stock II infinite transactions and saves O(k*N) work).
hints: If `k >= n / 2`, you can make as many transactions as you like (equivalent to Stock II).
Maintain arrays `buy[j]` and `sell[j]` for `1 <= j <= k`.
`buy[j] = max(buy[j], sell[j-1] - price)` and `sell[j] = max(sell[j], buy[j] + price)`.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
problems.statement:
You are given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i-th` day.

Find the maximum profit you can achieve. You may complete as many transactions as you like with the following restrictions:
- After you sell your stock, you cannot buy stock on the next day (i.e., cooldown one day).

Note: You may not engage in multiple transactions simultaneously.

examples.explanation: transactions = [buy, sell, cooldown, buy, sell], profit = (2-1) + (2-0) = 3.

commonMistakes: Buying on the cooldown day immediately following a sell.
Not allowing `rest` state to transition from previous rest.
hints: Model 3 states: `hold` (holding a stock), `sold` (sold stock today, enters cooldown tomorrow), `rest` (idle, can buy today).
`hold = max(prevHold, rest - price)`
`sold = prevHold + price`
`rest = max(rest, prevSold)`

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Transaction Fee
problems.statement:
You are given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i-th` day, and an integer `fee` representing a transaction fee.

Find the maximum profit you can achieve. You may complete as many transactions as you like, but you need to pay the transaction fee for each transaction.

Note: You may not engage in multiple transactions simultaneously (i.e., you must sell the stock before you buy again).

examples.explanation: Buy at 1, sell at 8, fee 2 = profit 5. Buy at 4, sell at 9, fee 2 = profit 3. Total 8.
Buy at 1, sell at 10, fee 3 = profit 6.

commonMistakes: Deducting the transaction fee both on buy and sell instead of once per completed transaction.
hints: Maintain two states: `cash` (max profit not holding stock) and `hold` (max profit holding stock).
`cash = max(cash, hold + prices[i] - fee)`
`hold = max(hold, cash - prices[i])`.

testCases.explanation: Stress test scale N=1000 for complexity verification
Stress test scale N=1500 for complexity verification

problems.title: Maximum Product Subarray
problems.statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, find a contiguous non-empty subarray within the array that has the largest product, and return the product.

The test cases are generated so that the answer will fit in a 32-bit integer.
constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: Two negative numbers multiply to a positive 24.

commonMistakes: Forgetting that multiplying a negative number by a previous negative minimum creates a positive maximum.
Zero resets product to 0.
hints: Track both `curMax` and `curMin` at each step because multiplying by a negative flips min and max.
When `nums[i] < 0`, swap `curMax` and `curMin`.
Update `curMax = max(nums[i], curMax * nums[i])` and `curMin = min(nums[i], curMin * nums[i])`.

testCases.explanation: Stress test scale N=100 for complexity verification
Stress test scale N=101 for complexity verification

problems.title: Maximum Subarray
problems.statement: Given an integer array `nums`, find the subarray with the largest sum, and return its sum.
commonMistakes: Initializing maxSum to 0 which fails when all numbers are negative.
hints: Kadane's algorithm: at each index, decide whether to add nums[i] to current sum or start fresh at nums[i].
`curSum = max(nums[i], curSum + nums[i])`.
`maxSum = max(maxSum, curSum)`.

problems.title: Maximum Sum Circular Subarray
problems.statement:
Given a circular integer array `nums` of length `n`, return the maximum possible sum of a non-empty subarray of `nums`.

A circular array means the end of the array connects to the beginning of the array. Formally, the next element of `nums[i]` is `nums[(i + 1) % n]` and the previous element of `nums[i]` is `nums[(i - 1 + n) % n]`.

A subarray may only include each element of the fixed buffer `nums` at most once.
commonMistakes: Failing to handle the case where all numbers are negative: totalSum - minSum yields 0 (empty set), which is invalid for non-empty subarray.
hints: A circular subarray with maximum sum is either a non-circular max subarray OR `totalSum - minSubarraySum`.
Use Kadane's algorithm to compute both maximum subarray sum and minimum subarray sum.
Special edge case: if `maxSum < 0`, all elements are negative, return `maxSum` directly.

testCases.explanation: Stress test scale N=1000 for complexity verification

problems.title: First Missing Positive
problems.statement:
Given an unsorted integer array `nums`, return the smallest positive integer that is not present in `nums`.

You must implement an algorithm that runs in `O(n)` time and uses `O(1)` auxiliary space.

examples.explanation: Numbers 1 and 2 are present, 3 is the smallest missing positive.

commonMistakes: Using `nums.indexOf` in a loop resulting in O(N^2)
Infinite while loop when duplicate elements exist (solved with `nums[nums[i] - 1] !== nums[i]`).
hints: In-place bucket sort: place each positive integer x (where 1 <= x <= n) at index x - 1.
Use while loop swapping nums[i] with nums[nums[i] - 1] until nums[i] is in correct spot or out of range.
Scan from 0 to n-1: the first index where nums[i] !== i + 1 gives answer i + 1.

problems.title: Find the Duplicate Number
problems.statement:
Given an array of integers `nums` containing `n + 1` integers where each integer is in the range `[1, n]` inclusive.

There is only one repeated number in `nums`, return this repeated number.

You must solve the problem without modifying the array `nums` and uses only constant extra space.

parameterDefinitions.name: nums
parameterDefinitions.description: Array of n+1 integers in range 1..n

constraints: All the integers in nums appear only once except for precisely one integer which appears two or more times.
commonMistakes: Modifying array in-place or sorting when constraint forbids array modification.
Using O(N) Set memory.
hints: Treat the array as a linked list where index i has pointer to nums[i].
Because of duplicate value, multiple nodes point to the same node, creating a cycle.
Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm detects the cycle entrance in O(N) time and O(1) space.

testCases.explanation: Stress test scale N=1501 for complexity verification
Stress test scale N=2000 for complexity verification

problems.title: Find All Duplicates in an Array
problems.statement:
Given an integer array `nums` of length `n` where all the integers of `nums` are in the range `[1, n]` and each integer appears once or twice, return an array of all the integers that appear twice.

You must write an algorithm that runs in `O(n)` time and uses only constant extra space (not counting the return array).
constraints: Each element in nums appears once or twice.
commonMistakes: Using `Math.abs` incorrectly after already negating indices.
hints: Use the array indices as a hash map: value x maps to index `|x| - 1`.
Negate the value at index `|x| - 1` to mark presence.
If `nums[|x| - 1]` is already negative, x is a duplicate!

Stress test scale N=1500 for complexity verification

problems.title: Set Mismatch
problems.statement:
You have a set of integers `s`, which originally contains all the numbers from `1` to `n`. Unfortunately, due to some error, one of the numbers in `s` got duplicated to another number in the set, which results in repetition of one number and loss of another number.

You are given an integer array `nums` representing the data status of this set after the error.

Find the number that occurs twice and the number that is missing and return them in the form of an array `[duplicate, missing]`.

parameterDefinitions.name: nums
parameterDefinitions.description: Array of integers with one duplicated and one missing

commonMistakes: Returning `[missing, dup]` instead of `[duplicate, missing]`.
hints: In-place sign negation: element x marks index `|x| - 1` as negative.
If index `|x| - 1` is already negative, x is the duplicate.
The index that remains positive at the end corresponds to the missing number.

problems.title: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards
problems.statement:
There are several cards arranged in a row, and each card has an associated number of points. The points are given in the integer array `cardPoints`.

In one step, you can take one card from the beginning or from the end of the row. You have to take exactly `k` cards.

Your score is the sum of the points of the cards you have taken. Given the integer array `cardPoints` and the integer `k`, return the maximum score you can obtain.

examples.explanation: Take 1 from beginning and 6, 1 from end: 1 + 6 + 1 = 8? Optimal is taking 3 from end: 5 + 6 + 1 = 12.

commonMistakes: Greedily picking the max of left and right at each step (fails on [1, 1000, 1]).
hints: Inverting the problem: taking k cards from ends is equivalent to leaving a contiguous subarray of size `n - k` with the MINIMUM sum.
Total sum minus minimum subarray sum of size `n - k` gives maximum score.
Use sliding window of size `n - k`.

testCases.explanation: Stress test scale N=2000 for complexity verification
Stress test scale N=2000 for complexity verification

problems.title: Maximum Length of Subarray With Positive Product
problems.statement:
Given an array of integers `nums`, find the maximum length of a subarray where the product of all its elements is positive.

A subarray of an array is a consecutive sequence of zero or more values taken out of that array.

Return the maximum length of a subarray with positive product.

examples.explanation: The product of all 4 elements is positive (24), length 4.
Longest subarray is [1,-2,-3] with product 6, length 3.
Single negative number product is negative, length 0.

commonMistakes: Resetting negative count on zero without resetting positive length.
Setting neg = pos + 1 before using previous pos value.
hints: Track `pos` (length of longest subarray ending at i with positive product) and `neg` (with negative product).
If `num > 0`: pos increases by 1, neg increases by 1 (if neg > 0).
If `num < 0`: pos becomes `neg > 0 ? neg + 1 : 0`, neg becomes `prevPos + 1`.
If `num === 0`: reset both pos and neg to 0.

problems.title: Non-decreasing Subsequences
problems.statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, return all the different possible non-decreasing subsequences of the given array with at least two elements. You may return the answer in any order (sorted lexicographically for deterministic testing).

Notice that the given array may contain duplicates, and two equal elements are considered non-decreasing.

examples.explanation: All 8 valid non-decreasing subsequences of length >= 2.
Only [4,4] has length >= 2 and is non-decreasing.
Subsequences must have at least two elements.

commonMistakes: Sorting the initial array (subsequence problems must preserve original ordering!).
Duplicate duplicate sequences generated without level-level used set.
hints: DO NOT sort nums — subsequences must maintain original array order.
Use backtracking. At each recursion level, maintain a `used` set of numbers to skip duplicate elements at the same tree depth.
Add path to result whenever `path.length >= 2`.
